chapter: Hopkins, Kelly's Stables and Red Allen
title: Playing vibraphone before pedals, and the burden of carrying it
summary: Early vibraphones had no damper pedal and were used for a few sustained notes in ballads; from 1933 to 1936 being hired for the vibes meant carrying two instruments for no extra pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So we jumped back to that. Now we want to jump forward again, because we missed a couple of things. When you -- for instance, we were talking about you going with Ella, but you went with Claude Hopkins before you did that.
Yeah, with -- well, how that one came about was because I played vibraphones.
You know? And well I started playing vibraphones back in '33.
Before they had pedals. So the vibraphones were --

The dampers turned, but the vibraphones at that time were used to hit the fifth of the chord, of the dominant, before, like the second eight, you play the first eight, and then you play -- like if it's in C, you hit a G, you know.
You did balance and things like that.
It was used for that, you know.
: Yeah, I see what you mean, yeah.
Sometimes you would hit a chord, but you couldn't stop it. But the dominant would always linger over because you were going into the relative chord anyway.
So if it lingered it sounded beautiful.
So that's when I started playing the vibes, you know, and it was written -- like Frank Skinner and people like that would write ballads with vibraphone notes.
Sometimes it would just be two or three notes I would play in the whole piece, but I would always be playing, mallets posed upon the vibraphones, and when I would
reach that note I would -- More like a symphony.

Yeah. So I played those, oh, I guess about from '33 until about '36, you know. When it got to the point where I had to carry them, when people would hire me because of the vibraphone. So that made me have to carry the vibes and the drums.
Which I thought was overbearing, which I didn't make any more money than the rest of the guys.
So I didn't think it was fair.
